name: Ruins of Zul'Mamwe
summary: Tucked away in a mountainous pocket south of the Mosh'Ogg Ogre Mound, the Ruins of Zul'Mamwe serve as a heavily fortified stronghold for the Skullsplitter troll tribe. Enclosed by steep cliffs on almost all sides, the ancient stone platforms now teem with fierce jungle trolls under the rule of their ruthless chieftain, Ana'thek the Cruel.

sections.title: Stronghold of the Skullsplitters
sections.body: The Ruins of Zul'Mamwe represent one of the primary seats of power for the Skullsplitter tribe in central Stranglethorn Vale. Cradled within a natural mountain amphitheater, the site has only a single open approach from the north, making it an exceptional defensive redoubt. From atop its weathered ziggurats and stone terraces, Chief Ana'thek the Cruel directs his warriors and witch doctors, defending their territory fiercely against both intruding adventurers and rival jungle troll tribes.

sections.title: Remnants of an Ancient Empire
sections.body: Like many of the stone settlements dotting the jungle, Zul'Mamwe is a relic of the ancient Gurubashi Empire that once held undisputed dominion over the southern reaches of the continent. Although the grand empire splintered long ago into squabbling, hostile factions, modern Skullsplitters fiercely guard these ancestral stones, continuing age-old tribal rituals amid the overgrown masonry and broken monoliths.

faq.q: Who controls the Ruins of Zul'Mamwe?
faq.answer: The ruins are held by the Skullsplitter troll tribe, one of the two dominant and aggressive jungle troll tribes in Stranglethorn Vale. They are commanded on-site by their chieftain, Ana'thek the Cruel.

Zul'Mamwe is located in central Stranglethorn Vale, just south of the Mosh'Ogg Ogre Mound. The encampment is enclosed by towering mountains on nearly every side, accessible primarily through a valley pass to the north.

faq.q: Why are the Skullsplitters hostile to travelers?
faq.answer: The Skullsplitter tribe is fiercely isolationist and hostile to outsiders, seeing all other races and rival troll tribes as trespassers on their ancestral lands. Led by the merciless Ana'thek the Cruel, they attack anyone who approaches their jungle sanctuary.

faq.q: What is the history behind these ruins?
faq.answer: The stone structures of Zul'Mamwe date back to the height of the Gurubashi Empire. Following the empire's collapse into warring splinter factions, the Skullsplitters claimed the site as an inland base of operations, preserving its ancient stone terraces.

angles.text: For Darkspear trolls aligned with the Horde, Zul'Mamwe stands as a sobering reminder of the savage, insular ways of their jungle kin who refused to abandon bloodthirsty traditions and adapt to the wider world.
